Operations.Name: KerberosRealmCreate
Operations.Description:
Create a new kerberos realm. This will be automatically populated during the
domain join process in an Active Directory environment. Kerberos realm names
are case-sensitive, but convention is to only use upper-case.

Entries for kdc, admin_server, and kpasswd_server are not required.
If they are unpopulated, then kerberos will use DNS srv records to
discover the correct servers. The option to hard-code them is provided
due to AD site discovery. Kerberos has no concept of Active Directory
sites. This means that middleware performs the site discovery and
sets the kerberos configuration based on the AD site.

Arguments.Name: data
Arguments.Description: Kerberos realm configuration data for creation.

Operations.Name: KerberosRealmDelete
Operations.Description: Delete a kerberos realm by ID.

Arguments.Name: id
Arguments.Description: ID of the Kerberos realm to delete.

Operations.Name: KerberosRealmUpdate
Operations.Description:
Update a kerberos realm by id. This will be automatically populated during the
domain join process in an Active Directory environment. Kerberos realm names
are case-sensitive, but convention is to only use upper-case.

Arguments.Name: id
Arguments.Description: ID of the Kerberos realm to update.

Models.Name: KerberosRealmCreateData
Models.Description: Kerberos realm configuration data for creation.

Fields.Name: AdminServer
Fields.Description: List of kerberos admin servers. If the list is empty then the kerberos     libraries will use DNS to look them up.

Fields.Name: Kdc
Fields.Description: List of kerberos domain controllers. If the list is empty then the kerberos     libraries will use DNS to look up KDCs. In some situations this is undesirable     as kerberos libraries are, for intance, not active directory site aware and so     may be suboptimal.

Fields.Name: KpasswdServer
Fields.Description: List of kerberos kpasswd servers. If the list is empty then DNS will be used     to look them up if needed.

Fields.Name: PrimaryKdc
Fields.Description: The master Kerberos domain controller for this realm. TrueNAS uses this as a fallback if it cannot get     credentials because of an invalid password. This can help in environments where the domain uses a hub-and-spoke     topology. Use this setting to reduce credential errors after TrueNAS automatically changes its machine password.

Fields.Name: Realm
Fields.Description: Kerberos realm name. This is external to TrueNAS and is case-sensitive.     The general convention for kerberos realms is that they are upper-case.
